subject: Food Science
title: Caramel Color
description: A fast breakdown of Caramel Color for builders.

hook.text: Caramel color is the world's most widely used food coloring. Cola, soy sauce, and bread all depend on it.

buildup.text: It's made by heating sugar with acids, alkalis, or ammonium compounds. Four classes exist—I through IV.

discovery.text: Class IV caramel color (ammonia-sulfite process) gives cola its brown. It's the most produced dye by volume.

twist.text: Class IV production creates 4-MEI, a potential carcinogen. California requires a warning label above 29 micrograms.

climax.text: Coca-Cola reformulated to reduce 4-MEI in California rather than put cancer warnings on its cans.

punchline.text: Cola changed its recipe to avoid a label. The color stayed. The chemistry shifted.

quiz.question: Why did Coca-Cola reformulate its caramel color for California?
options: To reduce 4-MEI below levels requiring cancer warning labels
